title: Grouping & Concept Stacking
description: Isolate sub-expressions using (...) to apply quantifiers, establish boundaries, and build production-ready patterns.

primer.definition: Parentheses group sub-patterns into distinct logical units. This allows you to apply quantifiers to multi-character blocks, enforce specific alternation boundaries, or extract structured components.
primer.goldenRule: Quantifiers and anchors placed directly outside a group apply to the entire expression inside the parentheses.
primer.mentalModel: Think of a group as a container that bundles several characters into one token. Once wrapped in (...), that whole block behaves like a single character for the purposes of quantifiers, alternation, and anchoring — the same way parentheses in arithmetic change what an operator applies to.
points: Parentheses create a capturing group by default: the text matched inside is remembered and can be extracted or referenced, not just grouped for repetition.
A quantifier placed immediately after a closing parenthesis repeats the entire grouped sub-pattern, not just the character before the parenthesis.
Alternation with | is scoped to the nearest enclosing group — (cat|dog) only chooses between 'cat' and 'dog', while an ungrouped cat|dog can split a larger surrounding pattern in half.
Groups are numbered left-to-right by their opening parenthesis, starting at 1, which matters once you have more than one group in a pattern.
pitfalls: Assuming a quantifier outside a group only repeats the last character inside it — (\d{2}){2} matches four digits total (two groups of two), not two digits repeated twice.

Forgetting to group alternation inside a larger pattern: ^GET|POST$ anchors 'GET' only at the start and 'POST' only at the end, which is not the same as ^(GET|POST)$ anchoring both options on both ends.
Treating every () as free — each capturing group adds an entry to the match result, so stacking groups you don't need to reference still changes what the match object returns.

examples.note: The + quantifier repeats the entire grouped unit 'ab', not just the letter 'b'.
Alternation inside parentheses is scoped to just the two listed options.
Two independent groups can sit side by side to capture separate structured components of one pattern.

cards.prompt: Bundle the text sequence 'ab' into a single reusable unit so it can be treated as a single token. Capture 'ab' in Group 1.
cards.hint: Wrap the exact characters inside parentheses: (ab).

cards.prompt: Isolate a 3-digit security code block into a single capture group so the numeric value can be extracted.
cards.hint: Combine the digit token \d{3} inside parentheses: (\d{3}).

cards.prompt: Filter animal records by matching either 'cat' or 'dog', scoping the choice inside a single group and capturing the matched animal name.
cards.hint: Use the vertical bar | inside parentheses: (cat|dog).

cards.prompt: Validate a 4-digit security token structured as two repeated 2-digit pairs, matching strictly from start to end. Capture the final repeated pair in Group 1.
cards.hint: Group two digits with (\d{2}), apply {2} to repeat the group, and anchor with ^ and $.

testCases.description: Rejects sequences with fewer than 4 total digits

cards.prompt: Identify high-priority log events by matching either 'LOG' or 'ERR', capturing the level name in Group 1.
cards.hint: Scope the options using (LOG|ERR).

cards.prompt: Validate software version tags that start with 'v' or 'ver' followed by one or more build digits, strictly from start to end. Capture the version prefix ('v' or 'ver') in Group 1.
cards.hint: Anchor with ^ and $, group the prefix options with (v|ver), and follow with \d+.

cards.prompt: Filter incoming HTTP requests by matching lines starting with either 'GET' or 'POST'. Capture the method name in Group 1.
cards.hint: Anchor at the start with ^ and scope method options inside (GET|POST).

cards.prompt: Parse configuration settings formatted as key=value strictly from start to end. Capture the word key in Group 1 and the numeric value in Group 2.
cards.hint: Anchor line with ^ and $, use (\w+) for the key, = for separator, and (\d+) for value.

cards.prompt: Parse log file entries starting with '[INFO]' or '[WARN]'. Capture only the inner level name ('INFO' or 'WARN') in Group 1, leaving out the square brackets.
cards.hint: Anchor with ^, escape brackets as \[\] and scope the text inside: \[(INFO|WARN)\].

cards.prompt: Parse date strings in DD-MM-YYYY format strictly from start to end. Capture the 2-digit day in Group 1, the 2-digit month in Group 2, and the 4-digit year in Group 3.
cards.hint: Use three independent digit groups (\d{2}), (\d{2}), and (\d{4}) separated by hyphens and anchored with ^ and $.

cards.prompt: Validate image upload paths by matching filenames ending with '.png', '.jpg', or '.gif'. Capture the extension name (excluding the leading dot) in Group 1 at the end of the line.
cards.hint: Escape the dot with \. and scope extension options inside (png|jpg|gif) anchored with $.

cards.prompt: Validate web addresses starting with 'http://' or 'https://'. Capture the protocol scheme ('http' or 'https') in Group 1 at the start of the line.
cards.hint: Anchor at start with ^, group protocol options (http|https), and follow with ://.

cards.prompt: Validate a segmented sequence consisting of a 2-digit number followed by a dot, repeated exactly 3 times strictly from start to end. Capture the final repeated segment in Group 1.
cards.hint: Group 2 digits and an escaped dot (\d{2}\.), apply {3}, and anchor with ^ and $.

testCases.description: Rejects sequences with fewer than 3 repetitions

cards.prompt: Validate employee identification badges starting with prefix 'ID' or 'CODE' followed by a hyphen and 4 digits, strictly from start to end. Capture the prefix in Group 1.
cards.hint: Scope prefix options with (ID|CODE), add hyphen -, follow with \d{4}, and anchor with ^ and $.

cards.prompt: Parse 24-hour timestamps in HH:MM format strictly from start to end. Capture the 2-digit hour in Group 1 and the 2-digit minute in Group 2.
cards.hint: Group hours (\d{2}) and minutes (\d{2}) separated by a colon :, anchored with ^ and $.

cards.prompt: Parse command-line inputs strictly from start to end, capturing the primary word command in Group 1 and all remaining arguments in Group 2.
cards.hint: Anchor with ^ and $, capture the first word with (\w+), match spaces with \s+, and capture remaining text with (.+).

cards.prompt: Validate standard IPv4 network addresses consisting of 3 repeated dot-terminated octets followed by a final octet, strictly from start to end. Capture only the repeated block sequence in Group 1 (leaving the final octet uncaptured outside of parentheses).
cards.hint: Combine (\d{1,3}\.){3} with a trailing \d{1,3}, anchored strictly with ^ and $.

testCases.description: Rejects incomplete IP addresses with missing octets
Rejects leading octet with more than 3 digits
Rejects middle octet with more than 3 digits
Rejects trailing octet with more than 3 digits

cards.prompt: Parse Social Security Numbers in XXX-XX-XXXX format strictly from start to end. Capture the 3-digit area code in Group 1, 2-digit group number in Group 2, and 4-digit serial number in Group 3.
cards.hint: Use three independent digit groups (\d{3}), (\d{2}), (\d{4}) separated by hyphens, anchored with ^ and $.

cards.prompt: Parse Semantic Versioning strings formatted as 'vX.Y.Z' strictly from start to end. Capture major version in Group 1, minor version in Group 2, and patch version in Group 3.
cards.hint: Start with literal v, wrap each digit section (\d+) in parentheses separated by escaped dots \., anchored with ^ and $.

cards.prompt: Parse price values formatted as '$XX.YY' strictly from start to end. Capture the integer dollar amount in Group 1 and the 2-digit cent amount in Group 2 (excluding the dot).
cards.hint: Escape the dollar sign \$, capture dollars with (\d+), match the dot \., and capture 2-digit cents with (\d{2}), anchored strictly with ^ and $.

testCases.description: Rejects price missing mandatory cent values

cards.prompt: Parse 2D integer coordinates formatted as '(X,Y)' strictly from start to end. Capture the X coordinate integer in Group 1 and the Y coordinate integer in Group 2.
cards.hint: Escape enclosing parentheses \( and \), capturing digits inside (\d+),(\d+) anchored with ^ and $.

cards.prompt: Parse phone numbers formatted as '(XXX) XXX-XXXX' strictly from start to end. Capture the 3-digit area code (without parentheses) in Group 1 and the 7 hyphenated subscriber digits in Group 2.
cards.hint: Escape parentheses around area code \((\d{3})\), add space \s+, and capture rest with (\d{3}-\d{4}) anchored with ^ and $.

testCases.description: Rejects missing space after area code

cards.prompt: Parse ISO calendar dates formatted as YYYY-MM-DD strictly from start to end. Capture the 4-digit year in Group 1, 2-digit month in Group 2, and 2-digit day in Group 3.
cards.hint: Anchor with ^ and $, creating three groups (\d{4}), (\d{2}), and (\d{2}) separated by hyphens.

cards.prompt: Parse REST API routing paths in the format '/version/resource', where the version is either 'v1' or 'v2'. Match the surrounding slashes outside your groups so Group 1 captures only the version string ('v1' or 'v2') and Group 2 captures the resource word.
cards.hint: Anchor with ^ and $, place literal slashes outside the groups as ^/(v1|v2)/(\w+)$, and extract 'v1' or 'v2' in Group 1.

testCases.description: Enforces $ anchor against trailing path segments
